sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.6,71,700/ for the damages caused to the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F4344 in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 30.11.2014 at about 6.50 a.m., the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F 4344 was in its schedule trip from MG Road to Shivajinagar in route number G11/2 and when bus reached near BRV Junction and at that time, one Durgamba Transport bus bearing Reg.No.KA51B2471 came in a rash SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2367/2020 and negligent manner and in high speed, without observing any traffic rules and regulations from the left side of the BMTC Bus and dashed against the left side of the BMTC Bus and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the said BMTC bus got damaged.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
For repairing the said vehicle, the Petitioner has spent total a sum of Rs.5,71,700/ towards repair charges and a sum of Rs.4,200/ per day towards loss to the Corporation from the date of accident.

The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Durgamba Transport bus bearing Reg.No.KA51B2471 by its driver and the Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No. 2 being the insurer of the Durgamba bus are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2367/2020 statement to the main Petition.
The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus and damages caused to the BMTC bus.

Further it contended that, the driver of the offending bus was driving vehicle cautiously with moderate speed,
so, there is no negligence on the part of the driver.
Further, it contended that the Respondent No.1 bus covered with insurance policy.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus and damage caused to the BMTC bus and expenses incurred for the repair of the said bus.
Further it contended that the insurer of the bus has settled the claim towards own damages from his insurance company.
Hence, the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2367/2020 Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

4. On the rival Pleadings, this Court has framed the following Issues:

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

6. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

7. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :

Issue No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioner that BMTC SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2367/2020 Bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F4344 got damaged in the Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 30.11.2014 at about 6.50 a.m., by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Durgamba Transport bus bearing Reg.No.KA51 B2471.

Ex.P4 to 6 are the Spot panchanama and Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and the Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.

The Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch shows the manner of the accident and the IMV report corroborates with the Petitioner contentions.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending bus by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
According to the Petitioner, due to the alleged accident, BMTC bus got damaged.

16. On perusal of IMV report which marked at Ex.P.7, the damages found to the BMTC bus bearing No.KA01F4344 are SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2367/2020 as under:
1. Front wind shield, front bumper, front cowl damaged.
2. Left side body and windows damaged between front and rear door damaged.
17. PW.1 has relied on Ex.P.9  Job card which shows the total cost required for repair of BMTC bus is Rs.5,71,700.26/.
Ex . P12
is the Certificate issued by the Depot Manager of Depot No.3, which shows the loss incurred for non using the said BMTC bus is Rs.4,200/.
It also shows the number of days which the said BMTC bus was not used is one day.

PW.2 who is the Depot Manager got marked the Certificate at Ex.P18 which shows that due to the said accident, the said BMTC bus sent for repair on 05.12.2014 and it returned after repair on 01.08.2015 and the said bus was not used for total 246 days and thereby they incurred loss of Rs.14,26,800/.
In his crossexamination he admitted that they kept Spare bus in every depot and if any bus got damaged, then, they will use the spare bus.
Further he admitted that he has not produced the original bill in SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2367/2020 supporting of Job card.
Further he admitted that he has not produced the separate bills for labour charges and he has not produced the separate bills to show the value of each parts and part number.
PW.1 has deposed in his crossexamination that he has not produced document to show that they spend Rs.5,71,700/ for the repair of their BMTC bus.
Further he deposed that he does not know whether he has produced document or not to show that their department incurred loss of Rs.4,200/ per day.

18. Though the Petitioner has deposed that they incurred total loss of Rs.6,71,700/ towards repair charges and the loss incurred during the period of repair, except Job card i.e., Ex.P.9 no other document produced before the Court to show they paid Rs.5,71,700.26/ towards repair charges and Ex.P18 i.e., Certificate to show that the said BMTC bus kept in garage for repair.
The said documents does not have supporting bills to show that the Petitioner had actually spent said amount towards the repair.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.
Hence, it is proper to award compensation to the Petitioner towards repair charges at Rs.5,71,700/ and loss of income at Rs.4,200/, in total Rs.5,75,900/.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,75,900/.

21. Issue No. 3 : In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
 SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2367/2020  ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,75,900/ along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the  Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, the same is ordered to be paid to SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2367/2020 the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.
1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
